rationale: IEP row: Id2 expression in cardiac crest/outflow tract is reported, and the experiment shows Id2 expression depends on neural crest (ablation reduces it), not that Id2 regulates crest formation; expression is not participation and no process replacement applies.
supporting_text: Cardiac neural crest ablation in the chick embryo, which causes structural defects of the cardiac outflow tract, results in a significant loss of Id2 expression in the outflow tract.

rationale: Sox9 morpholino knockdown after crest specification blocks trunk crest delamination and phosphorylated Sox9 cooperates with Snail2 to drive it, so Sox9 carries out the delamination step; the direct process term is more precise than positive regulation of crest cell differentiation.
supporting_text: Importantly, morpholino knockdown of Sox9 function after NC specification indicated that Sox9 is required for NC delamination.

rationale: Rgs2 loss induces formation of neural crest progenitors via derepressed Ppard-driven sox10 (crest specifier) transcription, i.e. Rgs2 restrains crest specification; it also promotes ectomesenchymal derivatives, so the generic negative regulation of crest differentiation would be misleading. Abstract only.
supporting_text: Disrupting Rgs2 expression by using a dominant negative rgs2 construct or rgs2 morpholinos reduced GTPase-activating protein activity, induced the formation of neural crest progenitors

replacement_labels: negative regulation of epithelial to mesenchymal transition
rationale: Tspan18 stabilises Cad6B protein in premigratory cranial crest to antagonise EMT, and its overexpression blocks migration; it has no reported effect on crest specification or differentiation, and GO has no regulation-of-crest-delamination term, so the generic EMT regulation term is the accurate replacement.
supporting_text: we conclude that Tspan18 post-translationally regulates Cad6B-dependent cell adhesion to antagonize cranial neural crest EMT
